hinge.title: Decide why Earth having a large amount of water does not mean there is plenty of water fit for everyday use.

intelligence.enrichment: Water covers about two-thirds of Earth's surface, but most of it is in oceans and seas as saline water. Saline water is not fit for domestic, agricultural, or industrial use, and freshwater sources are limited. If most available water is salty and only limited freshwater can be used, then water shortage can occur even on a planet with much surface water. The learner correctly applies this rule: Water covers about two-thirds of Earth's surface, but most of it is in oceans and seas as saline water. Saline water is not fit for domestic, agricultural, or industrial use, and freshwater sources are limited. Because Earth is covered with water, usable water is plentiful everywhere.
